question.text: A liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is added to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of a liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> at temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the temperature of the mixture becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. Now if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is added to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo></math> temperature of the mixture will be

solution.text:
Heat loss will always be equal to heat gain.

As per 1stcondition,

100×SA×(100-90)=50×SB×(90-75) ___(i)

As per 2nd condition,

100×SA(100-θ)=50×SB(θ-50) ___(ii)

Dividing (ii) by (i), we get
100-θ100-90=θ-5090-75

300-3θ=2θ-100

θ=80°C
